transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-06-02 16:00 PDT
- Duration: 38 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sara Nguyen (VelasHealth - Head of Privacy), Tom Ellis (VelasHealth - Infra), Priya Kapoor (VelasHealth - Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Weekly check-in focused on security/compliance items for the pilot: SSO setup, audit logging and retention, SOC2 paperwork, KMS/encryption, RBAC and staging demo. Action items and timelines captured.

Topics:
- SSO/SAML integration status
- Audit logs format, retention, and SIEM forwarding
- SOC2 evidence & pen test availability
- Data retention / PII handling during pilot
- KMS/HSM and key management questions
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um, quick roll call, we got Velas, Sara, Tom, Priya, and from Redwood it's Diego and me. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Sara: Good, thanks. On our side we've been going through the SSO steps, had a couple small questions, mostly around attribute mappings.
[00:18] Tom: Yep, infra is ready to accept SAML, we just need the metadata and expected cert rotation cadence.
[00:24] Maya: Great. Today's agenda is SSO, audit logs/retention, SOC2 docs, KMS and then agree next steps. Diego will demo the log config towards the end.
[00:34] Diego: Yeah, I'll try to get the staging view up, just a heads up though, staging doesn't have the full KMS plug in yet so you'll see the, uh, masked IDs.
[00:42] Priya: That's fine, as long as we can validate fields and retention. Our compliance team needs to confirm retention windows and export options.
[00:48] Sara: Also interested in what gets written to logs: is user prompt text included, or do you redact PII by default?
[00:56] Diego: Good question. By default in hosted POC we do full audit logs including request and response blobs, timestamps, model id, and route. We can enable masking for PII fields — it's a config flag. For Dedicated/Private, you control what we persist. Note there is a prefix/KV cache reference in the runtime, sometimes shows up as KV cash in the logs, sorry for the typo in the doc.
[01:16] Tom: When you say 'masking' is that token-level hashing, or removal? We integrate with Splunk/ELK and prefer hashed tokens so we can correlate without seeing raw PHI.
[01:26] Diego: Right — we have both options: reversible token hashing with customer-managed keys (KMS), or non-reversible redaction. For the pilot we can demo hashed tokens using our KMS integration, but full bring-your-own-key (BYOK) path is on the Private offering.
[01:40] Priya: BYOK is a blocker for us long-term, but for the POC we can accept hashed tokens if we can provide the KMS metadata later.
[01:48] Maya: Action item — we'll share the KMS/crypto design doc. I'll add that to the notes.
[01:52] Sara: Great. On SSO, we tried the metadata you sent but the NameID mapping didn't match our expected email attribute. Are you expecting 'mail' or 'userPrincipalName'?
[02:02] Diego: We expect email as the NameID by default but we can map to userPrincipalName. We'll include an optional attribute mapping table in the SAML guide.
[02:12] Tom: Also need to confirm cert rotation — what's your recommended cadence and how does Redwood handle expired certs during rotation?
[02:20] Maya: We recommend rotating every 90 days for customers with strict policies, but we support both manual and automated rotation. If certs expire we have fallbacks for a short window and alerts in the console. We'll share the SAML metadata with rotation notes.
[02:36] Sara: Cool. About SOC2 — do you have a current Type II report and recent pen test?
[02:42] Maya: Yes, we have a SOC2 Type II report as of 2025-03 and a summary of the most recent third-party penetration test. We'll share redacted reports today or tomorrow; full PDFs under NDA.
[02:52] Priya: We'll need the full report for legal review. Can you also include control mappings to our standard framework (ISO/PCI/GDPR notes)?
[02:58] Maya: We can provide a control mapping matrix, yes. I'll attach that.
[03:04] Tom: For audit logs — retention policy: what are the options in hosted POC? We may want 90 days staging, 365 logs for prod.
[03:12] Diego: Hosted POC default retention is 30 days, but configurable up to 365 for an account-level setting. For Dedicated we support longer retention and direct exports to your SIEM. We also support S3 export and on-demand snapshots.
[03:28] Priya: Is log integrity guaranteed? We need tamper-evidence for compliance.
[03:32] Diego: We sign logs server-side with an HMAC and can provide checksum files for each daily batch; for Dedicated we can integrate with your ledgering service.
[03:40] Sara: Does the audit log include system-level traces, e.g., which model variant was used, kernel selections, or just the model id?
[03:46] Diego: It includes model id and variant metadata, plus latency and token counts. Kernel selection is not in the standard log but we can add an optional metadata field — sometimes it's noisy, but useful for perf investigations.
[03:58] Tom: About SIEM forwarding — we need a sample log schema to map fields. Can you provide one?
[04:04] Diego: Yep, we'll include a sample JSON schema. I'll demo the staging logs now — bear with me while I share screen.
[04:12] [screen share noise / pause, 20s] 
[04:36] Diego: Okay I can show the audit log table, you can see timestamp, request_id, user_id (hashed), route, model_id, payload_size, tokens_in, tokens_out. Note the request/response blob is base64 encoded in the export.
[04:54] Priya: For Velas we need user_id to be consistent with our internal directory so hashing must be keyed by our salt; is that supported?
[05:02] Diego: We support customer-provided salt and KMS-wrapped key for hashing in Dedicated. In hosted we can accept a pre-hashed user id if you want to do the hashing client-side during the POC.
[05:14] Sara: Ok, we'll plan to pre-hash for now.
[05:19] Maya: Quick note on retention: we can configure per-route retention so PII-heavy routes get shorter retention. That might be useful for your triage flows.
[05:28] Tom: Nice. About data residency — our legal asks that logs remain in EU for EU traffic. Can Redwood partition logs by region during the pilot?
[05:36] Diego: Yes, we can route EU traffic to EU region and persist logs in that region for hosted; for Dedicated or Private you deploy in your VPC region. We'll include region routing policy docs.
[05:48] Priya: One more on RBAC — can we restrict who at Velas can view raw audit blobs? We need separation between operators and privacy reviewers.
[05:56] Diego: RBAC is supported in the console: roles like Viewer, Investigator, Admin. You can restrict 'view_raw_payload' permission. For hosted POC we'll demo role config in staging.
[06:08] Sara: Great. On legal side we also flagged retention deletion on user request (right to be forgotten). How do you handle deletes across caches and backups?
[06:18] Diego: We have a deletion propagation job; for hosted POC we do best-effort within SLA, and for Dedicated/Private you run the delete job inside your network. Backups are rotated and we can configure retention windows; for strict erasure we recommend Private deployment where you have filesystem-level control.
[06:36] Tom: Any artifacts we can get on deletion guarantees?
[06:40] Maya: We'll share the data retention & deletion playbook section.
[06:44] Priya: Moving to SOC2 specifics — we may need evidence for Incident Response and Change Management. Can you provide sample tickets or control evidence?
[06:54] Maya: We can provide a redacted incident log and changelog entries. Again full artifacts via NDA.
[07:02] Sara: About encryption at rest — do you use customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed keys in hosted?
[07:08] Diego: Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default. We have BYOK for Private and Dedicated. For the POC we can arrange a test where you pre-hash identifiers and we encrypt payloads at rest; full BYOK would come later.
[07:22] Tom: Can you give timeline for BYOK support on Dedicated?
[07:26] Maya: BYOK for Dedicated is available; for hosted it's limited. We'll include the support matrix in the doc.
[07:34] Priya: Any thoughts on pen test scope? We want to be sure third-party test covers exfil and lateral movement.
[07:42] Maya: Our last pen test covered web app auth, infra, and privilege escalation. We'll send the summary and scope; if you need a broader test we can coordinate.
[07:52] Diego: Back to logs demo — I'm toggling retention from 30 to 90 and you can see the policy applied per route. The staging console is a bit jittery, apologies, it's a POC environment.
[08:08] Sara: No worries. Can you show how to export to our S3 bucket for archive?
[08:12] Diego: Yep, just add the bucket ARN and the export policy; we can set up a delivery role. For now I'll paste an example export config in the chat.
[08:24] Tom: Please include the minimal IAM policy. We need least privilege.
[08:28] Diego: Will do.
[08:30] [brief cross-talk about scheduling] 
[08:40] Maya: Let's capture action items now. We've agreed to share SOC2 and pen test docs, SAML metadata + mapping, KMS design, sample log schema, and a staging demo of audit logs + retention.
[08:52] Sara: I'll also send our legal intake form so you can see what fields we need for evidence submission.
[08:58] Tom: We'll generate a quick list of SIEM fields and the endpoint.
[09:02] Priya: And I'll book the RBAC walkthrough — next Tuesday afternoon if that works for Redwood.
[09:08] Maya: Works for us.
[09:12] Diego: Quick note on instrumentation — if you want kernel-level telemetry (that sometimes shows model compile decisions) we'll need a separate perf session since it can be verbose.
[09:22] Tom: We might ask for that later during performance tuning.
[09:26] Sara: Anything else on compliance?
[09:28] Priya: No, that covers it.
[09:30] Maya: OK recap — next steps and owners in the notes. We'll send the SOC2 and pen test summary by tomorrow, SAML guide and metadata today, Diego will prepare the staging log demo by Friday, and Tom will share SIEM field list by Thursday, Priya and Maya will schedule the RBAC walkthrough for next Tuesday.
[09:52] Tom: Sounds good.
[09:54] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the CRM and share links.
[09:58] Sara: Thanks.
[10:00] End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional auto-caption errors (e.g. 'KV cash' for KV cache, 'S S O' spacing), minor speaker misattribution possible.
